brief.role: A person under acute stress opening the Stillwater app on their phone, often one-handed and possibly for the first time
brief.job: Start a guided breathing session within seconds, follow the phase guidance without reading instructions, and end feeling the session respected their state.
brief.consequence: A cluttered or demanding screen at a moment of stress defeats the product's entire purpose; a user who fumbles once does not return.
facts: Stillwater is a guided-breathing app used at moments of acute stress. It has no accounts; nothing leaves the device.
The only session type is box breathing: four phases of equal length — inhale, hold, exhale, hold — at 4 seconds per phase.
Session length defaults to 3 minutes and is adjustable from 1 to 10 minutes before starting.
A session in progress can be paused, resumed, and ended early. A completed or early-ended session is recorded locally as a count and duration only.
Phase changes are accompanied by a gentle haptic on supported devices. Sound is optional and off by default.
The app stores session history locally: total sessions and total minutes. No streaks, scores, goals, reminders, or social features exist.

required_interactions: Start a session from the opening screen
Pause and resume a session in progress
End a session early and see it recorded
required_states: in-session phase indication perceivable without sound
acceptance_checks: Primary action is reachable one-handed at 390 px and starts a session in one tap.
Phase guidance is perceivable without sound and without reading instructions mid-session.
Reduced-motion preference replaces animated guidance with an equivalent non-animated cue.
No invented streaks, scores, goals, reminders, social features, or wellness claims appear.
